historical_record.description: Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 175, McLaren Lodge.

Built of sandstone to designs by Edward R. Swain, Richardsonian Romanesque with a Mission Revival touch, as the park superintendent's residence and offices — the home of John McLaren, superintendent of Golden Gate Park for 53 years, a Scottish-born gardener trained on estates and at the Royal Botanic Garden in Edinburgh who came to California in 1872.

McLaren's report to the Park Commission on the earthquake's damage recorded that the lodge "had its chimneys thrown down and some minor cracks in the walls and some plaster is broke in the upper rooms."

The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract for alterations and additions to McLaren Lodge, to make it the new department's administration building, to William Horstmeyer Co. at $245,740, taking the alternate that faced the addition in brick instead of stone; the plans were by Kirby & Mulvin, architects.
The first Park Lodge, the keeper's house and office, was finished at the junction of the Avenue with the park, near the present lodge.
$44,833.83 was paid out for building the new Park Lodge.
With the new lodge finished, the old Park Lodge was sold for $300 and taken away, and its site planted with rhododendrons, azaleas and heaths.
Damaged by fire, and repaired with new tiles, hardware, paint and wiring.
